antibody-drug-conjugate.label: Antibody–drug conjugate
notes: ADCs: the conjugate is the primary test article; the linker-payload is assessed for genotoxicity and hERG separately.
ICH S9 applies (advanced cancer): abbreviated package; starting dose from 1/10 rodent STD10 or 1/6 non-rodent HNSTD rather than the NOAEL.

requirements.name: Anti-drug antibody assessment in toxicity studies
requirements.rationale: ADA must be measured to interpret exposure and findings; animal immunogenicity does not predict human immunogenicity

citation.text: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline S6(R1): Preclinical Safety Evaluation of Biotechnology-Derived Pharmaceuticals. Step 4 16 July 1997; Addendum Step 4, 12 June 2011.

requirements.name: Pharmacologically relevant species selection

citation.text: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline S6(R1): Preclinical Safety Evaluation of Biotechnology-Derived Pharmaceuticals. Step 4 16 July 1997; Addendum Step 4, 12 June 2011.

requirements.name: Repeat-dose toxicity in relevant species
requirements.rationale: S6(R1) section 4.4: duration follows the intended clinical use — generally 1 to 3 months, with 6 months supporting chronic use. S6(R1) gives no threshold that fixes one of those, so the duration is set by the programme rather than derived here (one relevant species identified: a single-species programme is acceptable)

cell-therapy.label: Cell therapy
notes: Cell and gene therapies fall outside ICH M3(R2); requirements follow FDA CBER and EMA ATMP guidance. A product-specific pre-IND (INTERACT) meeting is strongly advised.
ICH S9 applies (advanced cancer): abbreviated package; starting dose from 1/10 rodent STD10 or 1/6 non-rodent HNSTD rather than the NOAEL.

requirements.rationale: Distribution and persistence in target and non-target tissues, body fluids and gonads must be characterised before first human dosing

oligonucleotide.label: Oligonucleotide
notes: Synthetic oligonucleotide: the ICH small-molecule battery applies (OSWG), with the oligonucleotide class effects below assessed in addition. Repeat-dose tox is normally conducted in a rodent and a non-rodent (frequently non-human primate for antisense).
Genotoxicity: the standard ICH S2(R1) battery applies to synthetic oligonucleotides (OSWG 2013); backbone/sugar chemistry is considered when interpreting results.

requirements.name: Validated bioanalytical method for TK samples
requirements.rationale: Concentrations supporting regulatory decisions require a validated method

citation.text: Frazier KS. Antisense oligonucleotide therapies: the promise and the challenges from a toxicologic pathologist's perspective. Toxicol Pathol. 2015;43(1):78-89.

requirements.name: Tissue accumulation and reversibility (kidney, liver)
requirements.rationale: Oligonucleotides accumulate in highly perfused clearing organs; repeat-dose studies must characterise accumulation, the associated histopathology (e.g. basophilic granules, tubular changes) and its reversibility

requirements.name: Repeat-dose toxicity (non-rodent)
requirements.rationale: M3(R2) Table 1: trials between 2 weeks and 6 months are supported by studies of at least the same duration as the trial

requirements.rationale: A gene mutation assay is generally considered sufficient to support single-dose clinical trials

requirements.name: Local tolerance at the clinical route
requirements.rationale: Local tolerance is evaluated, preferably within general toxicity studies, by the intended clinical route

requirements.name: In vitro metabolic stability (liver microsomes)
requirements.rationale: In vitro metabolic data across species are expected before human exposure to support species selection and human clearance prediction

citation.text: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline M3(R2): Guidance on Nonclinical Safety Studies for the Conduct of Human Clinical Trials and Marketing Authorization for Pharmaceuticals. Step 4, 11 June 2009.

requirements.name: Plasma protein binding across species
requirements.rationale: Unbound fractions are needed to compare exposures across species and to compute free-drug safety margins

citation.text: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline S3A: Note for Guidance on Toxicokinetics: The Assessment of Systemic Exposure in Toxicity Studies. Step 4, 27 October 1994.

requirements.name: Toxicokinetics within repeat-dose studies
requirements.rationale: Systemic exposure must be measured in toxicity studies to relate findings to exposure; reported with the toxicity study (ICH M4S(R2) 4.2.3.2, 'including supportive toxicokinetics evaluations')

citation.text: Lindow M, Vornlocher HP, Riley D, et al. Assessing unintended hybridization-induced biological effects of oligonucleotides. Nat Biotechnol. 2012;30(10):920-923.

requirements.name: Hybridization-dependent off-target assessment (in silico + in vitro)
requirements.rationale: Sequence-complementary off-target transcripts are predicted in silico against the transcriptome and the credible candidates confirmed in vitro, so hybridization-dependent effects are understood before dosing humans

citation.text: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline M3(R2): Guidance on Nonclinical Safety Studies for the Conduct of Human Clinical Trials and Marketing Authorization for Pharmaceuticals. Step 4, 11 June 2009.

requirements.name: Primary pharmacodynamics (in vitro and in vivo)
requirements.rationale: Mechanism and pharmacologically active dose are needed to set the starting dose and to interpret toxicity

citation.text: Frazier KS. Antisense oligonucleotide therapies: the promise and the challenges from a toxicologic pathologist's perspective. Toxicol Pathol. 2015;43(1):78-89.

requirements.name: Pro-inflammatory and complement activation potential
requirements.rationale: Phosphorothioate oligonucleotides can activate complement and provoke pro-inflammatory responses; assess in vitro (complement split products, cytokines) and in the repeat-dose studies

citation.text: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline S7A: Safety Pharmacology Studies for Human Pharmaceuticals. Step 4, 8 November 2000.

requirements.name: Safety pharmacology core battery: CNS, cardiovascular, respiratory
requirements.rationale: The core battery must be completed before first administration in humans; it covers the central nervous (2.7.1), cardiovascular (2.7.2) and respiratory (2.7.3) systems

requirements.name: In vitro hERG (IKr) assay
requirements.rationale: An in vitro IKr assay is part of the S7B integrated risk assessment for delayed ventricular repolarisation

citation.text: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline S7B: The Nonclinical Evaluation of the Potential for Delayed Ventricular Repolarization (QT Interval Prolongation) by Human Pharmaceuticals. Step 4, 12 May 2005.

requirements.name: In vivo QT assessment in a non-rodent (telemetry)
requirements.rationale: An in vivo QT assay complements the in vitro IKr result; together they form the S7B integrated risk assessment

requirements.name: Chromosomal damage assay (in vitro or in vivo micronucleus)
requirements.rationale: An assessment of chromosomal damage in mammalian systems is added to support multiple-dose trials

citation.text: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline S2(R1): Guidance on Genotoxicity Testing and Data Interpretation for Pharmaceuticals Intended for Human Use. Step 4, 9 November 2011.

requirements.rationale: The complete standard battery should be finished before Phase 2

requirements.name: Immunotoxicity weight-of-evidence review
requirements.rationale: Standard toxicity data are evaluated for immunotoxic signals; dedicated studies such as TDAR are added only if signals are found

citation.text: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline M3(R2): Guidance on Nonclinical Safety Studies for the Conduct of Human Clinical Trials and Marketing Authorization for Pharmaceuticals. Step 4, 11 June 2009.

requirements.name: In vivo pharmacokinetics (ADME) in test species
requirements.rationale: Further information on pharmacokinetics (absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion) in test species should be available before exposing large numbers of human subjects or treating for long duration (generally before Phase III); exposure in the tox species before first-in-human is covered by toxicokinetics (ICH S3A)

citation.text: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline M3(R2): Guidance on Nonclinical Safety Studies for the Conduct of Human Clinical Trials and Marketing Authorization for Pharmaceuticals. Step 4, 11 June 2009.

requirements.name: Metabolite profiling and human metabolite comparison
requirements.rationale: Human metabolites at >10% of total drug-related exposure that are disproportionate to animals require nonclinical characterisation

citation.text: ICH Harmonised Guideline S10: Photosafety Evaluation of Pharmaceuticals. Step 4, 13 November 2013.

requirements.name: Photosafety assessment
requirements.rationale: Triggered if the molecule has a molar extinction coefficient greater than 1000 L/mol/cm at any wavelength between 290 and 700 nm

citation.text: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline M3(R2): Guidance on Nonclinical Safety Studies for the Conduct of Human Clinical Trials and Marketing Authorization for Pharmaceuticals. Step 4, 11 June 2009.

requirements.name: Embryo-fetal development (rat and rabbit)
requirements.rationale: Embryo-fetal assessment is required before inclusion of women of childbearing potential beyond the limited exposure M3(R2) permits (regional differences apply: EU and Japan expect it before any WOCBP exposure)

citation.text: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline M3(R2): Guidance on Nonclinical Safety Studies for the Conduct of Human Clinical Trials and Marketing Authorization for Pharmaceuticals. Step 4, 11 June 2009.

requirements.name: Fertility and early embryonic development
requirements.rationale: Male reproductive organs are evaluated in repeat-dose studies; a dedicated fertility study is expected before large-scale trials

requirements.name: Reproductive and developmental toxicity (oligonucleotide-adapted)
requirements.rationale: DART follows ICH S5(R3) adapted for oligonucleotides: species selection by pharmacological relevance and placental transfer, with class accumulation considered

citation.text: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline S1A: Guideline on the Need for Carcinogenicity Studies of Pharmaceuticals. Step 4, 29 November 1995.

requirements.name: Carcinogenicity assessment (2-year rat or S1B(R1) weight of evidence + rasH2 mouse)
requirements.rationale: S1A: carcinogenicity studies are performed for any pharmaceutical whose expected clinical use is continuous for at least 6 months; M3(R2) places them before the marketing application; under S1B(R1) a weight-of-evidence assessment may replace the 2-year rat study

vaccine.label: Vaccine
notes: Vaccine: evaluated under WHO TRS 927 and FDA vaccine guidance, largely outside the ICH S-series. Genotoxicity and carcinogenicity are not required for the antigen; a novel adjuvant is assessed separately (WHO 2013).

citation.text: World Health Organization. WHO guidelines on nonclinical evaluation of vaccines. WHO Technical Report Series No. 927, Annex 1, 2005.

requirements.name: Repeat-dose toxicity (full vaccination course + recovery)
requirements.rationale: One relevant species, the full clinical immunisation schedule plus one additional dose, with a recovery period and safety-pharmacology endpoints included
requirements.section: WHO TRS 927 Annex 1, section 4; FDA vaccine guidance

citation.text: World Health Organization. Guidelines on the nonclinical evaluation of vaccine adjuvants and adjuvanted vaccines. 2013.

requirements.name: Genotoxicity (antigen exempt; novel adjuvant/excipient only)
requirements.rationale: Genotoxicity is not required for the antigen; a novel adjuvant or novel excipient is assessed on its own merits

citation.text: World Health Organization. WHO guidelines on nonclinical evaluation of vaccines. WHO Technical Report Series No. 927, Annex 1, 2005.

requirements.name: Local tolerance at the injection site
requirements.rationale: Injection-site reactogenicity is evaluated, usually within the repeat-dose study rather than as a stand-alone study

citation.text: World Health Organization. WHO guidelines on nonclinical evaluation of vaccines. WHO Technical Report Series No. 927, Annex 1, 2005.

requirements.name: Biodistribution (nucleic-acid or vectored constructs)
requirements.rationale: DNA, mRNA/LNP and vectored vaccines require a biodistribution study; classical protein/polysaccharide antigens do not
requirements.section: WHO TRS 927 Annex 1; FDA guidance for DNA/vectored vaccines

citation.text: World Health Organization. WHO guidelines on nonclinical evaluation of vaccines. WHO Technical Report Series No. 927, Annex 1, 2005.

requirements.name: Immunogenicity (proof of immune response)
requirements.rationale: The nonclinical immune response (humoral and, where relevant, cell-mediated) in a relevant species is the primary pharmacology supporting a vaccine

requirements.section: FDA 2006 vaccine developmental-toxicity guidance; ICH S5(R3)
